mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates and increases equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive equity returns
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in FEDFUNDS < 2.0% periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPIAUCSL growth exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation, prompting central bank tightening that depresses equity valuations, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Inflation above 2.5% historically correlates with negative equity returns
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in CPIAUCSL yoy > 2.5% periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1200 thousand units, it signals a strong labor market and robust housing demand, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Strong labor and housing demand historically correlates with positive equity returns
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in UNRATE < 4.0% AND HOUST > 1200 periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 1.5% and remaining above for 3 months), central bank policy becomes restrictive, reducing equity valuations and causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Monetary tightening cycles historically correlate with negative equity returns
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in monetary tightening cycles are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceed 485,000 million dollars, it indicates strong consumer demand, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns through increased corporate earnings expectations.
evidence_refs: fact:Strong consumer demand historically correlates with positive short-term equity returns
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in RSAFS > 485000 periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a deteriorating labor market and potential recession, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings and risk aversion.
evidence_refs: fact:Unemployment above 4.5% historically correlates with negative equity returns
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in UNRATE > 4.5% periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 and housing starts (HOUST) drop below 1200 thousand units, it indicates a simultaneous supply shock and weak demand, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to recessionary fears.
evidence_refs: fact:Concurrent supply and demand weakness historically correlates with negative equity returns
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in INDPRO < 100 AND HOUST < 1200 periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns due to recessionary expectations.
evidence_refs: fact:Industrial production below 100 historically correlates with negative equity returns
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in INDPRO < 100 periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
